candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — standard precautions and PPE
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Standard Precautions PPE
candidate.educational_objective: Select appropriate face and eye PPE for anticipated blood/body-fluid splash or spray exposure.

options.A: A surgical mask alone even when the eyes may be exposed
options.B: Protective eyewear with a mask, or a face shield that protects the eyes, nose, and mouth, plus other task-indicated PPE
options.C: Gloves alone because mucous-membrane protection is unnecessary for splash risk
options.D: Eye protection only when the client specifically requests it

candidate.rationale: CDC Standard Precautions direct healthcare personnel to protect the mucous membranes of the eyes, nose, and mouth during procedures likely to generate splashes or sprays. CDC specifies protective eyewear plus a mask, or a face shield, selected according to the anticipated exposure and used with other indicated PPE. B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Standard Precautions require protection of eyes, nose, and mouth from anticipated splashes/sprays using protective eyewear plus a mask or a face shield, with task-appropriate PPE selection.
candidate.source_document_title: Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings
candidate.source_locator: Personal Protective Equipment section — use protective eyewear and a mask, or a face shield, for procedures/activities that could generate splashes or sprays
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: A nurse anticipates a procedure that may generate splashes or sprays of blood or body fluids toward the face. Which PPE approach is appropriate under Standard Precautions?
